Analysis: Hypothesis 1 offers a more novel and integrative approach by leveraging a 3D scaffold to trigger mechanotransductive signaling that leads to epigenetic reprogramming and restoration of cytochrome P450 expression. This pathway – linking mechanical cues directly to epigenetic modifications – is conceptually innovative and provides distinct experimental readouts. Although both hypotheses require more mechanistic detail and clear experimental parameters, Hypothesis 1’s focus on using intrinsic 3D environmental cues to enhance hepatocyte fidelity makes it slightly more plausible and amenable to tests that quantitatively assess epigenetic and metabolic changes. Its in vitro nature also presents a relatively safe setup, while the additional manipulation in Hypothesis 2 (targeted modulation of Wnt/β-catenin) risks ambiguity in the modulation strategy and a narrower focus on phase I enzymes. Overall, Hypothesis 1 is the superior concept.
